correctness.rationale: On the labelled crown graph the open-neighborhood sum at b_i is A-f(a_i), and similarly on the other side. The threshold is therefore exactly the two side-sum inequalities. A negative vertex sees all opposing 2's except a possibly matched one; cases of zero, one, and at least two opposing 2's give exactly the stated cell restrictions. The nine cells partition the n named pairs; their multinomial correctly counts labelings, without dividing by graph automorphisms. With a 2 on both sides each side has weight at least 3; if one side has no 2, it has weight at least 2 and the other side has only positive labels. For n>=5 this gives weight at least 7; for n=3 the no-2 side has odd weight and the only weight-six arrangement of this kind is all ones; for n=4, weight at most six would force the other side to be all ones, leaving no defending 2 on either side and hence all ones. Odd n>=3 attain six with two 2's per side and the indicated 1/-1 counts; even n>=4 attain it with one 2 per side in the same deleted matching pair. G_2 is a matching and its unique minimum is all ones. For n>=4, weight-three side profiles satisfy 3t+2u=n+3. Odd n forces a positive even t, so all pairs of side profiles are compatible. Even n permits a unique 2; each direction of a bad match has U_n D_n possibilities by symmetry and their intersection forces two distinct 2 positions and the binomial product J_n. Inclusion-exclusion proves the claimed minimum count. G_3 separately has nine pairings of two-2 side profiles plus all ones. A separate row-mask enumeration checked every full coefficient for n=2 through 7 against a sorted-multiset enumerator and recovered minima counts 1,10,84,900,3280,44100 (checks/frozen_checks.py argument 1; output checks/1.txt). Those finite checks corroborate rather than establish the universal formula.

broader_coverage.reasoning: For n>=3 nonadjacency fails to be an equivalence relation after ignoring equality: a_i and a_j are nonadjacent, a_j and b_j are nonadjacent, but a_i b_j is an edge for i!=j. Thus the multipartite formula does not apply, and G_2 is disconnected. The cited cubic equality is not an all-regular-graph enumerator.

value.rationale: The crown is a natural perturbation of the complete bipartite graph in this signed total-domination problem. The matching-pair compression replaces exponential enumeration in n with at most binom(n+8,8) cell profiles, and the parity law gives explicit degeneracies of the optimal labelings. These are useful extension data beyond the numerical invariant and comparison examples.
